why: broad emotional topic with an argument attached
posts:
A kid scored 3 goals across the tournament.

His name was not read out at the medal ceremony. He is not in the results. He came home and said he is not going back.

Children quit sport for reasons that have nothing to do with losing:

Reason 1: nobody noticed.

Most school tournaments keep no scorer list at all. The team wins, the captain gets the trophy, done.

Meanwhile that kid played the whole weekend hoping someone would say out loud that the goal was his.

Reason 2: it ended on day one.

Straight knockout with 20 teams. Lose once, you are finished.

Travelled all day, played 20 minutes, went home. He will not sign up for that again next year.

Reason 3: nobody understood who won or why.

The table existed only in the organiser's notebook. Who advanced, and on which tiebreaker, stayed a mystery.

A sense of unfairness lasts far longer in memory than a scoreline.

Three fixes, none of which cost money:

— A format where everyone plays every round instead of being knocked out first
— A scorer list, even handwritten on a wall
— A visible table, not one that lives only with you

A child's motivation does not run on trophies.

It runs on attention: the goal got recorded, the name is visible, a parent can look it up.

Attention is cheaper than a trophy and works harder. It is the single reason they come back next season.

If you have ever run a school tournament — did you keep a top scorer list?

In my experience it is missing about nine times out of ten. It is the cheapest opportunity in youth sport, and almost everyone skips it.
